title: G6: surface/manifold argument needs square boundaries to be embedded circles (depends on G2)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
`prop:s2` proves $|F_w|$ is a closed $2$-manifold via the link criterion. The 'interior of a $2$-cell' and 'interior of an edge' cases invoke regularity from `prop:W3` (each square embedded; each edge glued as a single facet of each incident square). The link-graph vertex computation is correct and was numerically confirmed (each $1$-cell on exactly two $2$-cells; vertex links are single cycles).

However the manifold conclusion requires that the **boundary of each square $T_m$ is an embedded circle** (a genuine $4$-cycle on four distinct corner $0$-cells with four distinct edges), not a square with identifications. `sec:attach` exhibits the $4$-cycles $Q_1\xrightarrow{}Q_2\xrightarrow{}Q_4\xrightarrow{}Q_5\xrightarrow{}Q_1$ etc., which DO have distinct vertices/edges; but the logical step 'therefore the characteristic map of the square is an embedding' relies on **G2** ('pairing determines isotopy class', issue prob-07-8) and on `lem:commute`. This dependency is not made explicit, and without G2 one cannot a priori exclude two distinct cubes mapping onto the same lower cell.

**Suggested fix.** After establishing G2, add one sentence: by uniqueness-up-to-isotopy the four corners and four edges of each square are pairwise distinct, so $\partial C(T_m)$ is an embedded $S^1$ and (with `lem:commute`) the square's characteristic map is an embedding; the link criterion then applies. Numerically verified: all four corners of each $T_m$ are distinct and each edge lies on exactly two squares.
